proposals.before: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Liao took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Yi took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
proposals.reason: Chinese 嶷 is the personal name Yi, not Liao; the English invents the wrong given name.

proposals.before: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Liao and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"
proposals.after: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"
proposals.reason: Same error as s0039: 嶷 should be Yi, not Liao.

proposals.after: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"

proposals.before: Young, Boyu served as acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's pacifier-army staff, as libationer of southern Xuzhou, and as acting adjutant on the stabilizing army of Prince Zixun of Jin'an.
proposals.after: Young, Boyu served as acting adjutant on Liu Yuanjing's pacifier-army staff, as libationer of southern Xuzhou, and as acting adjutant on the stabilizing army of Prince Zixun of Jin'an.
proposals.reason: Chinese 柳元景 is Liu Yuanjing; Yuanyuan is a mistranscription of 元景.

proposals.before: In youth Boyu was acting adjutant on Liu Yuanyuan's Pacifier Army staff, libationer of South Xuzhou, and acting adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's Stabilizing Army.
proposals.after: In youth Boyu was acting adjutant on Liu Yuanjing's Pacifier Army staff, libationer of South Xuzhou, and acting adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's Stabilizing Army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 柳元景 is Liu Yuanjing in the literal English as well.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before she had been capped.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Taishi, the fifteenth daughter of Prince of Jiangxia Yigong died at nineteen, before she had undergone the hairpin ceremony.
proposals.reason: 未笄 refers to the female hairpin coming-of-age rite, not male capping.

proposals.before: The monk Seng Zun was intimate with Mi and followed him to the prefecture; for a petty offense he was starved and held in the county jail. Seng Zun tore his three layers of clothing to feed him; when they were spent he died.
proposals.after: The monk Seng Zun was intimate with Mi and followed him to the prefecture; for a petty offense Seng Zun was starved and held in the county jail. He tore his three layers of clothing to eat; when they were spent he died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 食之 means Seng Zun ate his own torn robes while starving; the idiomatic invents feeding another person.

proposals.before: Shizu, as Prince of Yuzhang and Grand Commandant, named him staff adviser; his prefecture was unchanged.
proposals.after: Shizu transferred him to staff adviser under the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture was unchanged.
proposals.reason: 世祖轉爲豫章王太尉諮議 means Shizu reassigned Boyu to that post, not that Shizu himself became Prince of Yuzhang.

proposals.before: Shizu, now Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant, made him staff adviser; his prefecture stood as before.
proposals.after: Shizu transferred him to be staff adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture stood as before.
proposals.reason: The literal English wrongly makes Shizu into the Prince of Yuzhang.

decisions.reason: s0039 has 豫章王嶷; 嶷 is the given name Yi. English Liao is unsupported.
s0039 豫章王嶷 must be Prince of Yuzhang Yi in the literal field as well; Liao is wrong.
s0048 has 豫章王嶷; the same person as in s0039, so Yi not Liao.
s0048 詣豫章王嶷 requires Yi in the literal English; Liao invents the wrong name.
s0081 has 柳元景; 元景 is Yuanjing, not Yuanyuan.
s0081 柳元景 is Liu Yuanjing; the literal field must match.
s0012 未笄 of a 女 refers to the female hairpin rite (笄), not male capping (冠); s0014 confirms 女子十五而笄.
s0026 僧遵裂三衣食之 means Seng Zun tore and ate his own three robes; 食之 does not mean feeding another person.
s0137 世祖轉爲豫章王太尉諮議 means Shizu transferred Boyu to adviser under Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; Shizu is not himself that prince.
